title: Development and testing of a regionalization concept for the acute care of life-threatening infections on the basis of a telemedicine network
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, telemedical consultationfor intensive care units was set up in some places in Thuringia. This system allows medical staff from regional clinics to discuss a case with physicians of the Jena University Hospital. It is also possible to view the patient, device settings and findings via secure data lines. This concept is also being used after the pandemic to discuss serious illnesses. The telemedical consultation is now to be improved. To this end, certain diagnoses should always lead to a teleconsultation as early as possible. The aim is to determine as early as possible in the course of the illness whether the patient can remain on site or should be transferred to another hospital. This pilot is supposed to demonstrate feasibility of such concept.
conditions: Other symptoms and signs involving cognitive functions and awareness

interventions.name: Conduct of a teleconsultation for ICU patients when a trigger diagnosis is present
Historical control for ICU patients with a trigger diagnosis without teleconsultation (year 2019)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Predefined diagnoses of an ICU patient for initiation of teleconsultation within 24 of diagnosis:
sepsis or septic shock
severe ARDS
staphylococcus aureus bacteremia
endocarditis
acute or acute-on-chronic liver failure
acute loss of concsciousness
hospital desires a consultation for any reason
Exclusion criteria:
Patient or legal representative decline consultation of external physicians
